subject: Civil Engineering
title: Bridge Bearings: Letting Bridges Move
description: A 60-second lesson on Bridge Bearings: Letting Bridges Move.

hook.text: A bridge that can't move will crack itself apart from thermal stress.

buildup.text: Bearings sit between the deck and supports, allowing controlled movement.

discovery.text: Roller bearings allow horizontal sliding. Elastomeric pads flex in all directions.

twist.text: Some bearings are designed to break during earthquakes, isolating the deck from shock.

climax.text: Seismic isolation bearings saved Japan's highways during the 2011 earthquake.

punchline.text: The best bridges survive because they're allowed to move.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of bridge bearings?
options: To make the bridge look more aesthetically pleasing
To allow controlled movement between the deck and supports
To increase the total weight capacity of the bridge

details.summary: Bridge bearings are devices that support the deck on piers and abutments while allowing controlled movement from thermal expansion, traffic vibration, and seismic activity.
details.whyItMatters: Without bearings, thermal expansion alone could generate forces large enough to crack piers or buckle decks. Bearings are small components with outsized importance for bridge performance.
takeaways: Bearings allow controlled thermal expansion and contraction of the deck
Elastomeric pads deform to accommodate movement in short-span bridges
Locked bearings can cause catastrophic pier damage during earthquakes

faq.question: How much does a typical bridge deck expand from temperature changes?
faq.answer: A 100-meter steel bridge deck can expand about 60 millimeters between winter and summer temperature extremes. Concrete decks expand roughly half that amount. Without bearings to accommodate this movement, the forces generated would crack concrete piers or buckle steel connections.

faq.question: What happens when bridge bearings fail or seize up?
faq.answer: Seized bearings transmit forces the structure was not designed to resist, causing cracking in piers, damage to expansion joints, and uneven load distribution. In earthquakes, frozen bearings can cause pier failure. Regular inspection and replacement of worn bearings is essential for bridge safety.
